verdict.rationale: Capsule documents its own HTTPS REST API with Bearer-token auth, including self-generated tokens, and the product stores opportunities, pipelines, emails and notes. An agent could therefore plausibly pull this data to build a pre-meeting brief. However, the evidence never shows that the API exposes opportunities, emails or history, and there is no MCP server, llms.txt or OpenAPI spec (all probes returned 404). Missing for 10: documented API endpoints for opportunities, email and history/timeline data; an official MCP server; a machine-readable OpenAPI spec or llms.txt; any hands-on or independent evidence of an agent compiling an account brief.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent compile an account brief — open deals, recent emails, and history — from CRM data via the API or MCP server before a meeting

citations.quote: API requests are made via HTTPS using the `api.capsulecrm.com` subdomain. Each request must be authenticated with a user's Bearer token.
you can generate a token directly from your Capsule account to avoid the oAuth 2 flow.
Use Capsule's API to integrate with your custom or third party application.
